claims.statement: The root CMake project requires CMake 3.20, enables C++20, emits runtime artifacts under build/bin and libraries under build/lib, exports compile_commands.json, and declares application version 0.27.0.

The build uses CMake FetchContent with pinned references for imgui, implot, GLFW, Catch2, imgui_test_engine, imnodes, portable-file-dialogs, kissFFT, and nlohmann/json; dependencies are populated in the active build tree.
Windows builds are validated with MSYS2 MinGW-w64 and the repository does not support MSVC; changing compilers requires clearing the build directory because compiler detection is cached.

Installed runtime payloads place the executable, component_data, and extensions together under bin, while documentation is installed under share/doc/rf-simulator; CPack generates TGZ packages off Windows and ZIP packages on Windows.

The application resolves built-in component data and extensions relative to the executable, with source-tree fallback for build-tree runs; extension discovery also considers user and project-local roots with source built-ins taking precedence, and project-local tools are trust-gated.

LayoutManager stores the default layout at <exe_dir>/rf_simulator_layout.ini and named layouts under <exe_dir>/layouts; TutorialState stores completion at <exe_dir>/.tutorial_completed. SessionState persists app.ini next to the executable only on Windows and is a no-op elsewhere; .rfsim project files separately store a subset of window flags.

CTest discovers the main Catch2 test cases and registers standalone executables through add_standalone_test; because MinGW-w64 can silently drop cases from the main tests executable, release CI requires at least 223 registered cases on Windows and separate targets keep added coverage runnable.

Some CTest targets use RUN_SERIAL to protect shared executable-relative app state or mutable source-tree extension fixtures, but RUN_SERIAL applies only within one CTest invocation; separate concurrent invocations against the same build tree can still race.

The release workflow is tag-only: pull requests run no automated CI, while each v* tag is version/changelog-validated, runs formatting and AddressSanitizer, selects a strict-build matrix by tag class, tests optimized Release packages for both platforms, and creates a draft only after required jobs succeed.

The release preparation script requires a semantic version and changelog section, prepares a release branch by default or can operate on master, runs format/build/test gates unless skipped, and tag mode only tags a clean matching master commit.

The formatting script is the shared implementation for local and CI checks, requires clang-format 18, and supports changed-file reformatting, dry-run checking, full checked-set operations, and explicit files.

Enabling core.hooksPath activates local-only pre-commit clang-format, commit-subject, and non-fast-forward push checks; intentional history rewrites require the per-invocation RFSIM_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH override, and scripts/test-githooks.sh exercises the gates.

For release preparation on this Windows workstation, invoke scripts/release.sh with Git for Windows MSYS sh; after its sed version edit, verify the CMakeLists.txt diff is only the expected two-line change because line-ending normalization can otherwise rewrite the file.

The release job builds rf-simulator-linux-x86_64.tar.gz from exactly two root-level members, rf-simulator-linux copied from tiny-rf-simulator and rf-sim-mcp, and builds rf-simulator-windows-x86_64.zip with tiny-rf-simulator.exe, rf-sim-mcp.exe, and the MinGW DLLs inside one rf-simulator-windows folder.
The root and agent/mcp CMake files install tiny-rf-simulator and rf-sim-mcp into the bin destination, so they sit side by side in the install tree.

classify-release accepts only X.Y.Z tags; patch tags run one Linux GCC 14 Debug validation leg, while minor and major tags run four legs: Linux GCC 14 Debug, Linux GCC 14 Release, Linux Clang 18 Debug, and Windows MinGW-w64 Debug; every Linux leg configures with -DGLFW_BUILD_WAYLAND=OFF.
The format job runs the clang-format 18 check and the sanitizer job runs a Debug AddressSanitizer build with GCC 14 on every release tag, with the sanitizer CTest run excluding Benchmark and test_ui.

The strict-build and package jobs run CTest with Benchmark excluded, using xvfb-run on Linux, and the Windows legs also exclude test_ui because it drives an interactive window that cannot run headless.

The package job builds Release configurations for Linux GCC 14 and Windows MinGW-w64 and uploads tiny-rf-simulator, rf-sim-mcp, and the MinGW DLLs as artifacts that the release job packages into the release archives, so Debug builds are validation-only and never shipped.

The release job runs only when validate-version, format, sanitizer, package, and strict-build have all succeeded, generates its release body from the matching CHANGELOG section with scripts/release-notes.sh, and creates a draft GitHub release that attaches the Linux tarball and the Windows zip.
validate-version fails when the tag version differs from the CMakeLists.txt project version or when scripts/release-notes.sh fails for the tag.

scripts/release.sh prepare mode refuses a working tree with changes other than CHANGELOG.md and a version not greater than the current one, bumps the project VERSION line with sed, runs the gates unless --skip-gates is given, and commits CMakeLists.txt and CHANGELOG.md; tag mode refuses unless CMakeLists.txt is at the requested version, the tree is clean, and HEAD is on master, and then creates an annotated tag and pushes it.

scripts/install-clang-format.sh installs clang-format 18.1.8 with pip into the $HOME/.cache/clang-format-18 directory, where scripts/format.sh and the pre-commit hook look for it, when the system package manager does not provide clang-format-18.
imnodes, portable-file-dialogs, and kissFFT are fetched with FetchContent_Populate, so their upstream CMake files are not used.
